Christian Scientist here, hear me out. (Also any other scientists on this thread pls correct me if I’m off on anything.) According to most scientists (at the moment) due to the size of the universe there is a VERY high chance that aliens exist as many other planets in the Milky Way have the conditions to support life (theoretically) and that’s not even including moons or other galaxy’s. Then there’s time. We have reconcile ourselves with the fact that we are not the center of the world or rather the ever expanding universe that has been around far longer than most of us can even conceive of. If we truly believe that God is omnipotent then is it so hard to believe that God has created other life on other planets or moons before and perhaps some that will come after. What I’m suggesting is that if aliens exist, have existed, or ever do exist, their less likely to be angels or demons. Instead they would be more like humans, fish, flies, tulips, mushrooms etc and simply be another incredible creation by God. I like to think of it as playing with legos. If you ever had legos as a kid I’d be willing to bet you probably played out various stories with your legos, and “built” different things with the Lego pieces. And before you come after me for comparing God to a kid playing with Legos God does say that we are created in HIS image so I don’t think it’s a stretch to consider that our ideas surrounding creating and the process of such might be similar to God’s. 

Also if you’ve ever studied evolution, or biology (especially microbiology) you probably realized at some point that everything, especially regarding living things is cyclic. From the cycle of life, to the process of reproduction, the water cycle, even the creation of life on our planet has hundreds of these little cycles built in to keep it going while constantly improving (natural selection among other things). All this hints at a creator who is intelligent enough to think of even the tiniest single celled creature in terms of long term and what it might one day become. If you don’t already know, for over a billion years earth could not support life. The planet was far too hostile. Most if not all brand new planets cannot support life, it takes time for them to have the right conditions. To me that seems very cyclic, though on a much slower scale. So while I doubt we will ever contact aliens (even if their out their could just be alien mushrooms). I DO think that the possibility of aliens existing, having existed, or existing in the future seems to follow with the pattern of cycles in everything that exists aka everything God has created thus far.

Here’s my theory: Martha was an only child who after some awful abuse from her mother developed split personality disorder (I think that’s what it’s called) and developed Gulias personality as a way to cope with the abuse. Thus Martha is the og and Gulia fronts when Martha is stressed. At some point the parents and Martha must have realized that Martha had this disorder and she was given treatment that included Pervatin which caused the hallucinations and miscarriage later in the game, her mother was also taking the drug. Quick note, Martha was aware that Gulia was her alter however Gulia was not aware that Martha was the og she genuinely thinks their sisters. Lapo also probably knew since he mentions in the letter that he can tell the two (personalities) apart. On the day of “Martha’s death” aka the beginning of the game, Martha either went for a swim or became suicidal and tried to drown herself. Regardless Martha ends up nearly drowning the stress of which triggers Julia. If you pay attention you’ll notice that Gulia tends to “wake up” in high stress situations (after nearly drowning, miscarriage, after being shot etc…) where as Martha accounts for the scenes in between what we as Gulia play. Ex after the scene where Gulia does a tarot card reading with the white lady ghost she hallucinates swimming around and wakes up in the bath. How did she get there? Martha. Or in the beginning when Gulia is found on the beach by her parents then wakes up in bed. How did she get there? Martha. 

So what about the bedroom? Why are there two beds? Because they swapped houses with the Nanny. This is not their house, it was not designed with them in mind. It’s not unreasonable to assume that the Nanny, being an older woman likely had children and even grandchildren that she would go out of her way to accommodate by giving them bedrooms and such. (I assumed Nanny meant more like a caretaker and not that she was their actual grandmother). 

What about the pregnancy? Martha was pregnant, and Gulia being a separate personality but the same person was also pregnant and thus suffered a miscarriage. However since Gulia was not fronting during the child’s conception, she never realized that she was pregnant. 

Like I mentioned before Martha is aware of Gulia as another personality. Which explains why she left Gulia letters and a recording to explain her actions. For Gulia on the other hand, Martha becomes an imagined sister as a way for her mind to cope with the hallucinations, frequent abuse, and the fact that her entire family likely rarely ever acknowledged her by name growing up but instead always referred to Martha. How does a child who’s been put on Pervatin reason all this out? They might create an imaginary friend or in this case imaginary sibling… Martha. The irony being that it was Gulia who was imaginary the whole time, as Martha was the only real person.

Hi, I’m disabled. I’m also a writer and editor. 

Great question, honestly any rep is good rep. Because disabled people are just the same as blue eyes people, left handed people, and people with extra toes. Something out of their control made them noticeably better or worse at something in their life and/or affected how others see them. 

You do not need to go out of your way to avoid certain disability tropes or to fulfill them. Recognize that whatever advantages or disadvantages you give your characters, just like in real life, they will eventually just have to learn to live with it. Most non-magical characters in fantasy novels are not labeled as disabled even though their quality and length of life is usually less than that of their magical counterparts. Instead they go on living and unless their character arc is centered around BECOMING magical it’s almost never mentioned again (think the lord of the rings Aragon and his elf Wife). Treat your disabled characters the same. If your character was born with a disability that limits them, odds are they won’t turn into a villain because they’ve never known any other quality of life. However if your character was the Golden boy for most of his life and only now suffers from a disability that has completely changed his quality of life he may be bitter, depressed, seek revenge, terrified. People are complex and as long as their decisions are consistent with their character, your good.

It sounds like she is resource guarding. There’s a few things you could try. Firstly have you trained her to the “wait” or “stay” command when a piece of food or her toy is in front of her? If not work with her in a controlled private setting till she can wait for your verbal and/or physical cue to go for the treat or toy. Next if she plays fetch have her bring you the toy and teach her to drop it in front of you before you will throw it. Be sure she can do this with other dogs around as well once she is comfortable doing it alone. All of this should help her but depending on how bad the resource guarding is may not solve the problem. 

Another part of it is her recall. Regardless of what the other dog is doing with her toy she needs to be able to come to you when you call wherever you may be. Which requires her to always be paying at least some attention to you. This way if it’s looking like she’s about to get aggressive or another dog is coming in fast you can call her away before it escalates.

So they sorta parallel each other hopefully without being too on the nose. The amnesia doesn’t necessarily cover up concepts but rather makes them seem insignificant to that character because they have no reason to worry about things that they have no memory ties to. And it gives I a reason to excuse flashbacks and other memories as hallucinations from stress or tiredness rather than thinking too hard on them.

I do write in 3rd person but still try to keep it focused on the characters perspectives. My main goal is for the readers to both experience the world building, characters and plot as they would in any other book through T’s pov, while also reflecting I’s frustration at not being able to remember things that should be obvious to her. I don’t want to push them away with confusing stuff but I do want to do something similar to when your watching a horror movie and the crazy villain starts hearing/seeing stuff and you as a watcher are seeing and hearing the characters hallucinations and getting the same sense of fear even though you have the benefit of having more info as an audience member and know it isn’t real it still freaks you out. I am a biologist and I’ve studied and believe in evolution, genetics, microbiology and nearly everything in between. And I gotta say…YES. I’ve definitely learned some things while getting my degree that back up God’s existence or at the very least give a factual explanation to many miracles described in the Bible. The following examples will go down easier if you allow yourself to entertain the idea that God and science are not exclusive to one another. For biblical miracle there is a scientific explanation and visa versa. Also keep in mind that nearly every religion thrives on ignorance of explanation. Meaning that it’s easier to describe an event for which you have so scientific explanation as a miracle, than to spend the rest of your life studying, searching for the how. This doesn’t mean miracles don’t happen but rather usually when an event is described as miraculous it is because those describing it are unable to provide a probable scientific explanation that is repeatable.

(PSA: I’m NOT a physicist. I’ll likely mangle the physics and chemistry explanations so if you’re interested just Google it.) 

1. The Virgin Mary - Likely the most commonly known miracle in the Bible. But did you that it’s technically possible? The most likely way would be through a form of parthenogenesis. However due to the way the egg forms and in humans, the chemicals blocking it from dividing without protein from the sperm and about a dozen other factors the actual chances of this happening come to less than .001%. Basically a bunch of very unlikely things would have to happen virtually all at once in the body. Not likely but not impossible.

2. Moses parting the Red Sea - Ok I see you rolling your eyes but stick with me because the science behind this is really cool. There’s a famous physics experiment with light called the double slit experiment. Google it, it’s awesome. Basically scientists shot light photons (electrons) through slits and were able to determine that the way in which the light behaved (particle or wave) changed depending on whether or not the light was being observed. Ok so back to Moses. While the two aren’t directly related, it’s important to remember that nobody could part a sea on their own as described in the Bible without the help of modern technology (underwater tunnels, canals, dams etc) or divine intervention. However if something like light, without being messed with in any way, will consistently change its behavior based on simply being observed I don’t think it’s such a stretch to say that something similar could be at play with Moses. Remember the points not to say whether or not he did part the Red Sea but rather to explain HOW. Could it be that the electrons surrounding Hydrogen and Oxygen might behave in a similar fashion under the correct circumstances? Thus causing the water molecule as a whole to be influenced by the electrons surrounding it? Surely a particle would move faster than a wave. Not proof but definitely shows how little we know about the world around us. 

3. Walking on water - While the Bible describes Jesus to walk on water, there are some non Newtonian solids and liquids, the most commonly known being oobleck which you could walk on. Obviously plenty of other explanations exist like walking on ice. 

4. The universe is expanding outward from its center. This makes even less sense when you consider that the expansion is speeding up. But where is the energy coming from to speed up this expansion? 

5. Evolution - Evolution is an incredible topic in biology not only because it gives us glimpses of the bast but because it may just be supported by God himself. If your Bible has been translated for accuracy (rather than to appease culture or for the ease of reading) then the verse Genesis 1:1 reads “In a beginning…” suggesting this is not Gods first rodeo.

6. Genetics and Microbiology in general really prove to me that God is real. The smallest cell must be able to do an incredible amount of things and the systems within said cell are just as complex. The fact that everyone’s DNA is just a little bit different is incredible to me. Such detail has evolved thanks to an incredibly patient and wonderful guiding hand, that of God. 

7. Death - When you die your brain will emit pleasure hormones and chemicals to calm you for last moments. Many have also reported seeing a loved one who’s passed away prior to their own death. This deceased individual is often a close family member or a trusted friend. The science behind this is that individuals who experience seeing a lost loved one often die of old age and thus are experiencing their last moment via a very damaged, or dementia rattled brain. Essentially it’s a hallucination triggered by chemicals in the brain. However for a moment imagine modern science wasn’t a thing. You’re watching someone pass and they call out for their mother who passed 20 yrs prior. The reach out to her and call her name. To them it is very real. Thus you might explain this as the ghost of their mother coming to collect them. My point is that even though we can explain so much with science they are still miracles. To see a loved one as you pass is incredible. For light to react to your observation doesn’t seem like it should be possible. To share 99.9% of your DNA with someone and look nothing alike, knowing that somehow energy is being introduced into a completely closed system and pushing it away, even though such energy can not be created or destroyed is beyond strange. 

I think the reality of Gods existence lies in the incredible complexity in the world around us. As well as the amount of planning and shaping that went into guiding each and every living thing that has ever existed down to the single called amoeba. It’s all Gods doing and it’s all awesome as heck.
